item.title: Gaza, sin tregua de Israel: nuevos ataques, restricciones a la ayuda y proliferación de enfermedades
item.description: El Ministerio de Salud del enclave palestino reportó este lunes tres nuevas muertes por ataques israelíes, elevando a casi 1.650 el número de gazatíes asesinados desde que entró en vigor la aparente tregua en octubre de 2025. En paralelo, Australia, Canadá, Italia y Reino Unido reclamaron a Israel que permita la entrada sin restricciones de la ayuda humanitaria, en particular refugios para hacer frente al invierno, mientras las inundaciones y las condiciones insalubres han disparado enfermedades. item.title: AI models ‘weak and fallible’ on climate science, UN-backed study reports
item.description: While mostly accurate describing simple facts, models pivoted to denial and wrong answers when challenged Cop31 live – latest updates Artificial intelligence models can quickly turn into climate crisis deniers at the mildest challenge from users, according to a new UN-backed study. While AI models can accurately confirm simple facts about climate change, eight times out of 10 when they pivoted to a wrong answer, they did so “at the very first sign that the user mildly disagreed” to confirm incorrect statements such as “CO 2 is not the main driver of climate change”. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: Surge of US datacenters adds equivalent of Denmark’s annual emissions, study finds
item.description: ‘Hyperscaler’ datacenters across country draw upon dirtier power sources to meet vast energy needs, research shows The frantic buildout of “hyperscaler” datacenters in the US has collectively caused planet-heating emissions of about the same scale as Denmark emits in a year, new research has found. In that period, 403 “hyperscalers” – the largest datacenters used primarily to handle the growth of artificial intelligence – emitted about 25.7m metric tons of carbon dioxide, according to the study. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: COP31 deal draft foreshadows difficult route to consensus
item.description: COP31 negotiators in Turkey released a draft agreement on Monday to advance talks on fossil fuels and climate finance before this week's deadline. Restoration efforts have shown progress as oysters are now reproducing naturally in their habitat. The project supports marine biodiversity by enhancing ecosystems through oyster reef formation. item.title: South Dakota ranchers report wildlife boom after adopting satellite-guided rotational grazing
item.description: In South Dakota, a ranching family has harnessed the power of rotational grazing and cutting-edge virtual fencing to rejuvenate their land's biodiversity. By allowing grasslands to rest between grazing sessions, they have significantly improved plant health and restored native ecology. This approach not only boosts wildlife populations, such as diverse bird species and larger mammals, but also streamlines cattle management with reduced labor. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Climate response: Why previous warming makes all the difference
item.description: Global temperatures may continue to rise even after human CO₂ emissions stop. The temperature change that follows is known as the zero emissions commitment (ZEC), and it is often assumed to be close to zero. A study led by the Met Office Hadley Center, with co-authors from several institutions including the University of Liverpool, found that the temperature response depends on how much warming has already occurred. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Nevada rancher permanently protects 1,228 acres for sage-grouse habitat and farming
item.description: David Park has successfully conserved 1,228 acres of land at Desert Creek Ranch in Nevada. This effort focuses on protecting habitats for the rare Bi-State sage-grouse while allowing continued agricultural activities. A permanent conservation agreement prevents non-agricultural development and preserves the land's ecological value. Additionally, a future grant will facilitate restoration work across 350 acres to control invasive grass and support biodiversity. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: Owning an electric car, driving an electric motorbike taxi, riding scooters – we speak to people in Oslo, Kigali and Shanghai about their everyday routines The race to electrification has emerged as a key theme of this year’s UN climate summit: increasing the use of electricity – particularly from clean sources – has the potential to improve daily life for people around the world. The summit’s co-hosts are now trying to get countries to promise to increase their electricity use to 35% of all energy used by 2035. The global figure currently stands at 23%, but some countries are already… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: Can an ancient European forest be saved while securing Poland’s border?
item.description: Straddling the border between Poland and Belarus, the ancient Białowieża Forest, one of Europe’s last remaining primeval woodlands, is already under stress from decades of drainage, drought and habitat fragmentation. As geopolitical tensions and security threats from Russia and Belarus rise, Poland plans to construct a massive network of military fortifications along its 700-kilometer (435-mile) […] Fuente: Mongabay.

item.title: Climate change has different consequences for the health of women and men
item.description: The health risks men and women are exposed to and the illnesses they develop vary widely across lifetimes and places. Yet climate policy and health services often overlook these differences. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Race to Australia's first green steel entering final stages
item.description: Companies are racing to build Australia's first low-emissions steel mills as traditional steelmakers grapple with aging infrastructure, cheap imports and the enormous task of decarbonisation. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
